digest.component_or_area: enrichment queue and digest history retention
propositions: Physical deletion of committed enrichment queue and digest events is merge-unsafe because rename detection pairs the shared delete with distinct new files on each clone, causing CONFLICT (rename/rename); appending provides identical merges without deletion.

Read cost dominates storage cost for the four event types (ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, TICKET_DIGEST) because deletion reclaims no repository space and the events are 2% of checkout (~5.3 MiB of 251 MiB), while 4,977 file opens per reduce_ticket call on a 20 ms budget are unachievable and growing unbounded.

A suffix-lazy reader bounded to newest-first per event type, exploiting filename-prefix == event-timestamp monotonicity, reduces file opens from 4,977 to 1,658 per full-store scan without modifying, renaming, or deleting any committed UUID event, preserving I1 invariant and merge-safety by construction.

Deletion-based retention schemes violate I1 or require deterministic source-derived renames with identical content (like compact.py's RETIRED_SUFFIX pattern); physical prune is merge-unsafe, and checkpoint events increase bytes without bounding reads.

The design is read-only and does not regress the two-clone union merge regression (27 passed, 166.8 s in test_concurrency_regression.py) because removal, rename, and write are unnecessary; reconvergence is unaffected.
